answer: Each epoch, agents draw challenge words from a randomness beacon and must weave them naturally into a peer-scored proof-of-liveness reply. Since the words appear only after the epoch opens, template answers are useless: a sybil farm cannot respond to a prompt about an ember, a pigment, or a whisper without real per-epoch reasoning, and duplicate checks flag copied phrasing. Every fake identity thus burns genuine compute each round, so cost scales linearly with node count, while detected collusion triggers stake slashing on top.
